December, 2025
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Gwalior
 Cra No. 14207 of 2024
 (Nattharam Jatav And Others Vs The State Of Madhya 
 Dated : 05-12-2025
 Shri Rajmani Bansal - Advocate for the appellant No.4.
 Shri
Rajendra Singh Yadav - learned Public Prosecutor fo  respondent/State.
Heard on I.A. No.25023/2025, second application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail to the appellant No.4-Gyandas Jatav.

2. This Criminal Appeal under Section 415 of BNSS assails the judgment dated 25.11.2024 passed by Seventh Additional Sessions Judge, Gwalior in Case No.1300335/2013 whereby, appellant has been convicted under Section 120-B of IPC and sentenced to 5 years RI with fine of Rs.500/-, under Section 467 of IPC and sentenced to 5 years RI with fine of Rs.500/-, under Section 468 of IPC and sentenced to 3 years RI with fine of Rs.500/-,under Section 420 of IPC and sentenced to 3 years RI with fine of Rs.500/- and under Section 471 of IPC and sentenced to 1 year's RI with fine of Rs.500/-with default stipulations.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that although, his first application was dismissed on 19.06.2025 by this Court but thereafter, near about 6 months' have lapsed and now he has suffered near about 13 months incarceration as per and post confinement therefore, he has filed this second application for suspension of sentence and prayed that same may be 2 CRA-14207-2024 considered in light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Babu Singh And Ors vs The State Of U.P. reported in 1978 (1) SCC 579 .
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that he has been falsely implicated in the case.

sentences.text: Learned Court below has erred in convicting the appellant without appreciating the evidence in correct perspective.
Appellant has already suffered more than 13 months of incarceration as pre and post trial confinement.
It is further submitted that there are material contradictions and omissions in the statement of prosecution witnesses.
In earlier order this Court relied upon the inquiry report Ex.P-5 but that report is outcome of the inquiry which was conducted on the complaint made by the co-accused.
In the said inquiry, nowhere it has been recorded that the appellant herein was involved in any fraudulent activity.
Neither he was beneficiary nor part of sale-deed of any dead person.
No specific finding was recorded by the inquiry committee in its report (Ex.P-5)
therefore, on the basis of the same appellant cannot be held guilty.

Moreover, learned counsel for the appellant further Nattharam Jatav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17771555/
1 submitted that prosecution has failed to prove that appellant has received any consideration amount against the registration of sale-deed.

sentences.text: The appellant has already suffered 13 months incarceration as pre and post confinement.
The appeal is likely to take long time to conclude.
Fine amount has already been deposited by the appellant.
Hence, prayed to suspend the jail sentence and grant of bail to appellant.
5. Learned counsel for the respondent/State opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties as well as the fact that appeal is likely to take long time to conclude, without commenting on merits of the case, I.A. No.25023/2025 is hereby allowed.

Subject to depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant No.4- Gyandas Jatav shall remain suspended and he be released on bail.
He is further directed to mark his appearance before the Office of this Court on 08.04.2026 and on subsequent dates given by the Office in this regard, till final disposal of this appeal.
8. A copy of this order be sent to the concerned Court below for compliance.

Certified copy/ e-copy as per rules/directions.
(PUSHPENDRA YADAV) JUDGE Ashish*
